# Maison Prisma Aurum

> A portfolio proof of concept by Michael Mas for a fictional luxury house, Maison Prisma Aurum: a dark 3D salon where visitors walk between pedestals, customize products (three glasses, a lipstick, a face paint, a watch, a ring, a hair color, headwear) and try them on live with their webcam or on a photo from their device, alone or as a whole look. The interface is in English and French, a procedural concierge android guides visitors from piece to piece and talks with them, and glazed doors behind the entrance open onto a contemporary art gallery: interactive procedural works, a kinetic installation, and a theatre where three automatons perform a mechanical ballet with live-synthesized music, moving lights and a director's camera, a webcam brass mirror, and a passport that unlocks Gold and Mirror collections for every piece. Everything runs in the browser: WebGPU rendering with a WebGL2 fallback, face tracking with MediaPipe in WebAssembly, no server and no third-party requests.

- Source code and full technical write-up: https://github.com/michael-mas/3d-virtual-store
- Author: Michael Mas (https://github.com/michael-mas)

## Technical highlights

- Next.js App Router static export, TypeScript strict, deployed on Vercel.
- React Three Fiber on three.js `WebGPURenderer`; a single persistent canvas, modes swap scene content.
- Materials and post-processing written in TSL (three.js shading language): transmissive and iridescent lenses, holographic shaders, lipstick lit from the video's own luminance, neon face paint with additive halos.
- Try-on: MediaPipe Face Landmarker (478 landmarks, blendshapes) and Hand Landmarker (21 landmarks, loaded only for hand products) and a hair segmenter (hair color) served locally; rigid products follow the facial transformation matrix with a head occluder; makeup is drawn on a face mesh rebuilt from the landmarks every frame, with masks authored in canonical-face UV space; watches and rings are pinned to the hand, back-projected from the image landmarks with a metric scale from a typical palm size.
- Products are data: a registry entry defines attachment type, customization schema and pricing; the customizer UI and cart are generated from it.
- All 3D models are generated by code (glTF + Draco), including three procedural glasses frames.
- Quality: unit tests (Vitest), end-to-end tests (Playwright) running the full loop in CI, strict Content Security Policy, zero external runtime requests.
